hook.text: Line up four or six cylinders in a row and you get the most common engine layout on Earth.

buildup.text: The inline-four is simple, compact, and cheap—perfect for daily drivers worldwide.

discovery.text: The inline-six is naturally balanced, producing silky-smooth power without extra counterweights.

twist.text: BMW built its reputation on inline-sixes, treating the smooth layout as a brand signature.

climax.text: Most modern cars use inline-fours because they fit sideways in front-wheel-drive layouts.

punchline.text: The simplest layout became the world's most popular engine.

quiz.question: Why is the inline-six naturally smooth?
options: Its firing order is inherently balanced

details.summary: Inline engines arrange all cylinders in a single row, creating a simple, compact layout that is the most common engine configuration in cars, ranging from three-cylinder economy engines to smooth inline-six performance units.
details.whyItMatters: The inline layout is the default engine architecture because of its simplicity and manufacturing economy. The inline-six in particular offers perfect primary and secondary balance for exceptional smoothness.
takeaways: All cylinders are arranged in a single row along the crankshaft
Inline-four is the most common car engine configuration worldwide
Inline-six engines are naturally balanced and exceptionally smooth

faq.question: Why is the inline-four so popular?
faq.answer: It is the simplest multi-cylinder layout, with only one cylinder head, one set of valvetrain components, and straightforward manufacturing. The four-cylinder offers a good balance between power, fuel economy, and cost.

faq.question: Why is the inline-six considered the ideal engine layout?
faq.answer: With six evenly spaced firing intervals per two crankshaft rotations, the inline-six has perfect primary and secondary balance. This inherent smoothness eliminates the need for balance shafts required by four-cylinder engines.
